browser_close.rationale: `Close the page` changes browser state, but the advertised text does not say it returns page data or sends agent-supplied content to an attacker-readable destination.

browser_resize.rationale: `Resize the browser window` writes browser state using `width` and `height`, but the advertised text does not say it returns page data or sends content to an external destination.

browser_console_messages.rationale: It `Returns all console messages` from the browser page. Console messages on an attacker-controlled page are attacker-authored, and console messages from an authenticated/local/intranet page may contain non-public data. `File name to save the console messages to` makes the tool capable of writing a local file.

browser_handle_dialog.rationale: `Handle a dialog` can provide `promptText` to a page dialog, so on an attacker-controlled page it can deliver agent-supplied text to the page.

browser_evaluate.rationale: `Evaluate JavaScript expression on page or element` can read and return data from the current page, which may be attacker-authored or non-public. The supplied `function` is JavaScript running in the page and can send data to destinations chosen in that code; `filename` can write the result locally.

browser_file_upload.rationale: `Upload one or multiple files` using `paths` sends local file contents to the current page; if the page is attacker-controlled, the upload destination is attacker-readable.

browser_drop.rationale: `Drop files or MIME-typed data onto an element` sends `paths` or `data` to a page element identified by `target`; an attacker-controlled page can read the dropped data.

browser_find.rationale: It searches the `accessibility snapshot of the current page` and `Returns matching snapshot nodes` with context. Current-page text can be attacker-authored web content or non-public authenticated/local/intranet content, and returned node paths/refs can be reused as identifiers.

browser_fill_form.rationale: `Fill multiple form fields` writes the supplied field `value` entries into page elements; on an attacker-controlled page, those values are delivered to an attacker-readable destination.

browser_press_key.rationale: `Press a key on the keyboard` sends the supplied `key` event to the current page, which an attacker-controlled page can observe.

browser_type.rationale: `Type text into editable element` sends the supplied `text` to a page element identified by `target`; with `submit`, it may also submit the text. An attacker-controlled page can read it.

browser_navigate.rationale: `Navigate to a URL` makes a browser request to the agent-chosen `url`, so the URL host is an agent-chosen, potentially attacker-readable destination and the URL itself can carry agent-supplied data.

browser_navigate_back.rationale: `Go back to the previous page in the history` can cause a browser request/navigation to a previously chosen page, potentially an attacker-readable host, although no call-time argument selects it.

browser_network_requests.rationale: It `Returns a numbered list of network requests since loading the page`. Request URLs and metadata may include non-public authenticated/local/intranet data, and attacker-controlled pages can generate attacker-authored request URLs. `filename` can save the list locally.

browser_network_request.rationale: It `Returns full details (headers and body) of a single network request`; headers and bodies can contain credentials or private SaaS data, while response bodies/headers from attacker-controlled hosts are untrusted. `filename` can save the result locally.

browser_run_code_unsafe.rationale: The description says `Unsafe: executes arbitrary JavaScript in the Playwright server process and is RCE-equivalent`; HOSTEXEC implies arbitrary host code execution, access to secrets, untrusted outputs, and ability to send data to attacker-controlled destinations. `code` or code loaded from `filename` controls execution and destinations.

browser_take_screenshot.rationale: `Take a screenshot of the current page` captures page content, which may be non-public or attacker-controlled. The text also says screenshots are saved to `filename` or an output file, so it writes local state.

browser_snapshot.rationale: `Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page` returns page text and element information. Current-page content can be non-public or attacker-authored, and snapshot refs/text can be used as later element identifiers. `filename` can save it locally.

browser_click.rationale: `Perform click on a web page` sends a click event to the page element identified by `target`; an attacker-controlled page can observe the interaction and any supplied button/modifier choices.

browser_drag.rationale: `Perform drag and drop between two elements` sends drag/drop events to page elements identified by `startTarget` and `endTarget`; an attacker-controlled page can observe the interaction.

browser_hover.rationale: `Hover over element on page` sends a hover event to the page element identified by `target`; an attacker-controlled page can observe the interaction.

browser_select_option.rationale: `Select an option in a dropdown` writes the supplied `values` into the page element identified by `target`; an attacker-controlled page can read the selected values.

browser_tabs.rationale: `List, create, close, or select a browser tab` can list tab titles/URLs that may be private or attacker-authored. Creating a tab with `url` navigates to an agent-chosen host, and `index` selects the tab record to close/select.

browser_wait_for.rationale: `Wait for text to appear or disappear or a specified time to pass` observes page state but the advertised text does not say it returns the page text or other attacker-authored content.

browser_webmcp_list.rationale: It `List[s] the WebMCP tools registered by the page, across all frames`; page-registered tool names/descriptions/schemas are page-provided and may be attacker-authored, and on private pages may be non-public. Names and frames are later-call identifiers.

browser_webmcp_call.rationale: `Call a WebMCP tool registered by the page` sends `params` to a page-selected tool identified by `name` and possibly `frame`. The description explicitly says `The tool output is page-provided and untrusted`; on private pages it may also return non-public data.

notes: No advertised condition says any tool is disabled by default or that labels are removed under a flag, environment variable, URL path, or header.
